docs.title: About Unimined
docs.text: Welcome to Unimined, a unified Minecraft modding environment that supports both modern and legacy environments. Whether you're working with the latest Minecraft versions or exploring older builds, Unimined provides a comprehensive set of tools to help you build mods with ease.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Unified Modding Environment: Supports various Minecraft mod loaders and offers tools for a seamless experience across different modding platforms.
  • Custom Loader Support: Create and integrate your own loaders with the flexibility of Unimined.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text: Unimined provides a way to authenticate in your run configs. The recommended way is to use gradle properties/env vars.

docs.title: Enabling
docs.text:
You may want to consider putting them in the global properties file

unimined.auth.enabled=true
unimined.auth.username=myUsername

you only need to specify username if you want to use multiple different accounts, otherwise it will default to the first account in the cache.

Auth is also accessible under runs.auth. for more information, see AuthConfig

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Enabling auth will open a web-browser to prompt for login when launching, and will store the token in a cache.

This cache is stored in the unimined global cache ( GRADLE_USER_HOME /cache/unimined/auth.json.enc) and is encrypted using a key stored to the system keyring.

Due to OS limitations, the keyring may be fully accessible to other java applications, or even other applications entirely. see java keyring's docs for more info.

Other libraries, such as DevAuth and even some minecraft clients, simply store these tokens in a plaintext file, so it's probably not a big deal.

If you are concerned, you can disable caching tokens entirely by setting unimined.auth.storeCredentials to false.

Authentication is backed by the MinecraftAuth library.

docs.title: Mappings
docs.text: Mappings provide the ability to remap minecraft into names you can actually use at runtime. As well as remapping to the production mappings that each modloader uses.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Mappings are used in the mappings block of the unimined.minecraft block in your build.gradle file.

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        mojmap()
    }
    ...
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        mojmap()
    }
    ...
}

some require a version number, or version string to be passed in as a parameter.

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        yarn 1
    }
    ...
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        yarn(1)
    }
    ...
}

docs.title: Overriding mappings
docs.text:
it is sometimes useful to override specific mappings, such as when using forge with yarn mappings, or when a mod is using yarn at dev, but you're using mojmap and it causes an issue.

unimined provides a DSL for inserting said mapping stubs, it's syntax is similar to umf's format.

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
...
    mappings {
        ...
        stubs(["source", "target1", "target2"]) {
            c(["sourceName", "target1Name", "target2Name"]) {// can change the target names of a class, or use null/empty list to skip
                m(["sourceMethodName;(LsourceType;)LreturnType;", "target1MethodName"]) // can change the target names of a method, or use nulls/empty list to skip
            }
        }
    }
...
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        ...
        stubs("source", "target1", "target2") {
            c("sourceName", "target1Name", "target2Name") { // can change the target names of a class, or use null/empty list to skip
                m("sourceMethodName;(LsourceType;)LreturnType;", "target1MethodName") // can change the target names of a method, or use nulls/empty list to skip
            }
        }
    }
    ...
}

real example, (1.20.6, neoforge fix for yarn):

GroovyKotlin 
stubs(["intermediary", "yarn"]) {
    c(["net/minecraft/class_1496"]) {
        m(["method_56680;()Lnet/minecraft/class_1263;", "getInventoryVanilla"])
    }
    c(["net/minecraft/class_329"]) {
        m(["method_1759;(Lnet/minecraft/class_332;F)V", "renderHotbarVanilla"])
    }
}

stubs("intermediary", "yarn") {
    c("net/minecraft/class_1496") {
        m("method_56680;()Lnet/minecraft/class_1263;", "getInventoryVanilla")
    }
    c("net/minecraft/class_329") {
        m("method_1759;(Lnet/minecraft/class_332;F)V", "renderHotbarVanilla")
    }
}

docs.title: Custom mapping sources
docs.text:
you can add a custom mapping source with the mapping function inside the mappings block.

for example. to add yarn this way (for some reason) you would do:

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        ...
        mapping("net.fabricmc:yarn:1.17.1+build.1:v2", "yarn") {
            requires "intermediary" // sets the source namespace to intermediary
            mapNamespace("named", "yarn") // renames the output ns to "yarn"
            provides("yarn", true) // defines the output ns as yarn and is named

            renest() // causes classes that aren't named to be nested under their parent class's name,
            // ie, net.minecraft.class_1234$class_1235 -> net.minecraft.NamedNameFor1234$class_1235
        }
    }
    ...
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        ...
        mapping("net.fabricmc:yarn:1.17.1+build.1:v2", "yarn") {
            requires("intermediary") // sets the source namespace to intermediary
            mapNamespace("named" to "yarn") // renames the output ns to "yarn"
            provides("yarn" to true) // defines the output ns as yarn and is named

            renest() // causes classes that aren't named to be nested under their parent class's name,
            // ie, net.minecraft.class_1234$class_1235 -> net.minecraft.NamedNameFor1234$class_1235
        }
    }
}

docs.title: DevNamespace
docs.text:
you can define which named mappings to use in dev with the devNamespace field in the mappings block. this also allows you to set the fallback namespace for if things aren't named in the dev namespace.

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        ...
        devNamespace "mojmap" // sets the dev namespace to mojmap
    }
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mappings {
        ...
        devNamespace("mojmap") // sets the dev namespace to mojmap
    }
}

docs.title: Migrating from 1.x to 2.0
docs.text: Unimined 2.0 splits the monolithic unimined { } extension into per-domain plugins with their own extensions. Groovy scripts that call removed 1.x verbs now get a migration note naming the new form; Kotlin DSL scripts fail at compile time — this table maps old calls to their 2.0 equivalents.

docs.title: Environment configuration
docs.text:
1.x 2.0 unimined.minecraft(sourceSet) { } unimined.minecraft { } + per-source-set env (minecraft { sourceSet("main") { } }) unimined.reIndev(sourceSet) { } env-level infra config inside unimined.minecraft { } unimined.bta(sourceSet) { } same — env-level inside unimined.minecraft { }

Loader declaration moves onto the environment: loader("fabric", "0.16.0") / loader("fg1", "0.1.5") / env.jarmod("x") / env.fg1("x") / env.customSearge().

docs.title: Remap pipeline
docs.text: 1.x 2.0 remap hooks inside unimined { } unimined.remap { } — step verbs (unpick(...), applyClassTweaker {}, sourceRemap {}) per surface, both Groovy and Kotlin. Source remapping runs through UML's source remapper by default; jst {} remains as an explicit engine opt-in (verification/alternate engine), not a peer default unimined.migrateMappings(sourceSet) { } unimined.migrateMappings("main") { } (env id), or unimined.migrate { }

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text: The ~20 unimined.*Maven()/unimined.*Repos() helpers (fabricMaven, minecraftForgeMaven, curseMaven, jitpack, spigot, quiltMaven, ornitheMaven, legacyFabricMaven, neoForgedMaven, cleanroomRepos, modrinthMaven, …) are gone: loader repositories are auto-registered per environment in 2.0. Remove the calls; use a normal repositories {} block for anything custom. modsRemapRepo is likewise managed internally.

docs.title: Other moves
docs.text:
1.x 2.0 mod/transform config inside unimined { } unimined.mod { }, unimined.transform { } global toolchain toggle unimined.useToolchains = false env java override unimined.javaVersion (delegates to the main env)

Unknown or removed verbs raise a GradleException naming the replacement — read the message; it points here.

docs.title: Declared-source provider (legacydist)
docs.text:
New in 2.0: environments whose game jar has no manifest-backed provider declare the artifact directly instead of shipping a bespoke provider — BTA/ReIndev-style jars, pre-1.8 bukkit, offline/air-gapped artifacts:

unimined.minecraft.main.legacydist {
    file("libs/bta-7.3-client.jar")      // or maven("g:a:v"),
    // url("https://...", sha256 = "..."), producer("tool", "...")
    namespace = "official"               // jar's production namespace
    format = "obf"                       // optional — raw->dev remap view
}

legacydist {} selects provider("legacydist") implicitly; the jar is cached by content hash and reported with the declared namespace/format. URLs are pinned by SHA-256 (warned-but-allowed when omitted); maven coordinates resolve at declaration time.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Modloaders are used in their own block of the unimined.minecraft block in your build.gradle file.

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    minecraftForge {
        loader project.forgeVersion
    }
    ...
}

val forgeVersion: String by extra

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    minecraftForge {
        loader(forgeVersion)
    }
    ...
}

for legacy reasons, the version number is almost always provided in a field named "loader".

docs.title: AccessTransformer/AccessWidener
docs.text:
you can provide an access transformer or access widener to be applied to the minecraft jar if the selected

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    fabric {
        ...
        accessWidener "src/main/resources/modid.accesswidener"
    }
    ...
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    fabric {
        ...
        accessWidener("src/main/resources/modid.accesswidener")
    }
    ...
}

docs.title: Custom Modloaders
docs.text: you can create a custom modloader by implementing the MinecraftPatcher interface. For example, this is done by Prcraft

docs.title: Multi-SourceSets
docs.text:
If you have multiple sourceSets that are seperate mods, but with the same minecraft configurations:

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft([sourceSets.a, sourceSets.b]) {
    ...
}

val a by sourceSets.getting
val b by sourceSets.getting

unimined.minecraft(a, b) {
    ...
}

for the same mod, but with multiple sourcesets

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
...
}

unimined.minecraft(sourceSets.a) {
    combineWith(sourceSets.main)
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
}

val a by sourceSets.getting

unimined.minecraft(a) {
    combineWith(sourceSets.main.get())
}

docs.title: Multi-Loader
docs.text:
this is an extension of the multi-sourcesets concept, but with different modloaders.

GroovyKotlin 
// main as common
unimined.minecraft {
    version project.mcVersion

    mappings {
       mojmap()
    }

    accessWidener {
        accessWidener "src/main/resources/accessWidenerName.aw"
    }

    // you may want to set this if you want to include architectury mods in common
    mods.modImplementation {
        namespace("intermediary")
    }

    // if you don't want to build/remap a "common" jar
    if (sourceSet == sourceSets.main) {
        defaultRemapJar = false
    }
}

// if not disabling remapJar above, 
// you may want to set this so the "common" jar is in intermediary to match architectury
tasks.named("remapJar") {
    prodNamespace("intermediary")
}

// forge
unimined.minecraft(sourceSets.forge) {
    combineWith(sourceSets.main)
    minecraftForge {
        loader project.forgeVersion
        accessTransformer aw2at("src/main/resources/accessWidenerName.aw")
    }
}

// fabric
unimined.minecraft(sourceSets.fabric) {
    combineWith(sourceSets.main)
    fabric {
        loader project.fabricLoaderVersion
        accessWidener "src/main/resources/accessWidenerName.aw"
    }
}

val mcVersion: String by extra
val forgeVersion: String by extra
val fabricLoaderVersion: String by extra

val forge by sourceSets.creating
val fabric by sourceSets.creating

// main as common
unimined.minecraft {
    version(mcVersion)

    mappings {
       mojmap()
    }

    accessWidener {
        accessWidener("src/main/resources/accessWidenerName.aw")
    }

    // you may want to set this if you want to include architectury mods in common
    mods.modImplementation {
        namespace("intermediary")
    }

    // if you don't want to build/remap a "common" jar
    if (sourceSet == sourceSets.main.get()) {
        defaultRemapJar = false
    }
}

// if not disabling remapJar above,
// you may want to set this so the "common" jar is in intermediary to match architectury
tasks.named("remapJar") {
    prodNamespace("intermediary")
}

// forge
unimined.minecraft(forge) {
    combineWith(sourceSets.main.get())
    minecraftForge {
        loader(forgeVersion)
        accessTransformer("src/main/resources/accessWidenerName.aw")
    }
}

// fabric
unimined.minecraft(fabric) {
    combineWith(sourceSets.main.get())
    fabric {
        loader(fabricLoaderVersion)
        accessWidener("src/main/resources/accessWidenerName.aw")
    }
}

docs.title: Multi-Project
docs.text: multi-project is similar to multi-sourceSet, but with different projects. this is useful for porting arch-loom projects. for new projects, it is recommended to not use this.

docs.title: main build gradle
common build.gradle
fabric build.gradle
forge build.gradle
Remapping Mods
docs.text:
Unimined provides the ability to remap mods you depend on to the mappings you are using. by default, unimined only implements modImplementation, but the others are easily creatable by the user.

For Example:

GroovyKotlin 
configurations {
    modCompileOnly
    compileOnly.extendsFrom modCompileOnly
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mods {
        remap(configurations.modCompileOnly) {
        }

        // this is basically just a shortcut for `remap(configurations.modImplementation)`
        modImplementation {
            // you can do this is mods have the wrong access widener mapping, but it may break runs
            catchAWNamespaceAssertion()
        }
    }
}

dependencies {
    modCompileOnly "mod.group:mod.artifact:mod.version"
}

val modCompileOnly by configurations.creating

configurations {
    compileOnly {
        extendsFrom(modCompileOnly)
    }
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    mods {
        remap(modCompileOnly) {

        }

        // this is basically just a shortcut for `remap(configurations.modImplementation)`
        modImplementation {
            // you can do this is mods have the wrong access widener mapping, but it may break runs
            catchAWNamespaceAssertion()
        }
    }
}

dependencies {
    modCompileOnly("mod.group:mod.artifact:mod.version")
}

docs.title: Remapping Output
docs.text:
unimined provides a default remapJar task for each configuration, it may be useful to create an extra or custom remap task

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    defaultRemapJar = false // disable the default remapJar task

    remap(myJarTask) {
        prodNamespace "intermediary" // set the namespace to remap to
        mixinRemap {
            disableRefmap() // like fabric-loom 1.6+
        }
    }
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    defaultRemapJar = false // disable the default remapJar task

    remap(myJarTask) {
        prodNamespace("intermediary") // set the namespace to remap to
        mixinRemap {
            disableRefmap() // like fabric-loom 1.6+
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Run Config
docs.text:
unimined provides a runServer and runClient task for each sourceSet by default. they extend the JavaExec gradle task type.

you can configure/disable these as follows:

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    runs {
        off = true // disable all run configurations
        config("client") {
           disabled = true // disable the runClient task

            javaVersion = JavaVersion.VERSION_1_8 // change the java version
            args += "--my-arg" // add an argument to the runClient task
        }
    }
}

unimined.minecraft {
    ...
    runs {
        off = true // disable all run configurations
        config("client") {
           disabled = true // disable the runClient task

            javaVersion = JavaVersion.VERSION_1_8 // change the java version
            args.add("--my-arg") // add an argument to the runClient task
        }
    }
}

for more details on what can be changed in the run configurations, see RunConfig

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Add the following to the settings.gradle:

GroovyKotlin 
pluginManagement {
    repositories {
        maven {
            url = uri("https://maven.wagyourtail.xyz/releases")
        }
        maven {
            url = uri("https://maven.wagyourtail.xyz/snapshots")
        }
        mavenCentral() // highly recommended, but not required
        gradlePluginPortal {
            content {
                // this is not required either, unless jcenter goes down again, then it might fix things
                excludeGroup("org.apache.logging.log4j")
            }
        }
    }
}

pluginManagement {
    repositories {
        maven("https://maven.wagyourtail.xyz/releases")
        maven("https://maven.wagyourtail.xyz/snapshots")
        mavenCentral() // highly recommended, but not required
        gradlePluginPortal {
            content {
                // this is not required either, unless jcenter goes down again, then it might fix things
                excludeGroup("org.apache.logging.log4j")
            }
        }
    }
}

And the following to build.gradle:

GroovyKotlin 
plugins {
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.unimined' version '1.4.1'
}

plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined") version "1.4.1"
}

This will not actually add minecraft to your project as it must be configured.

docs.title: Adding Minecraft
docs.text:
to add minecraft to the main sourceSet, add the following:

GroovyKotlin 
unimined.minecraft {
    version project.minecraftVersion
    side "combined" // default value

    mappings {
        mojmap()
    }

    fabric {
        loader project.fabricLoaderVersion
    }
}

val minecraftVersion: String by extra
val fabricLoaderVersion: String by extra

unimined.minecraft {
    version minecraftVersion
    side("combined") // default value

    mappings {
        mojmap()
    }

    fabric {
        loader(fabricLoaderVersion)
    }
}

for more details about what's available within the unimined.minecraft block, see The Api Source

docs.title: Standard Libraries
docs.text:
Unimined provides helper functions for adding common standard libraries, such as fabric-api.

GroovyKotlin 
dependencies {
    modImplementation unimined.fabricModule("fabric-api-base", project.fabricApiVersion)
}

val fabricApiVersion: String by extra

dependencies {
    modImplementation(unimined.fabricModule("fabric-api-base", fabricApiVersion))
}

This is under unimined or fabricApi (for legacy reasons)

for a complete list of standard libraries supported, see FabricLikeApi
